Public buildings, Nova Scotia-Sydney Mines,

Sydney is the headquarters of the Nova Scotia Steel and Coal Company, and is a very important place of 4,000 inhabitants. They have been pressing strongly for further accommodation. The proposed public touilding will toe used for a post office, custom-house and other government purposes. Judging from the cost of buildings elsewhere, I should think the total toost 'would toe between $15,000 and $20,000.
speakername: The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS (Hon. James Sutherland).

speechtext: Has the site been obtained V
No; there has not been any previous vote for tills work.
The building will be erected by tender and contract, 1 suppose ?
Yes.
No site has been chosen, no plans prepared, and no estimate made as to the cost, except that It will not exceed $15,000 or $20,000-that is all the information we can get.
We can hardly buy the site, or go to the expense of preparing plans or making estimates until we have a preliminary vote by parliament.
At any rate, that is all the information that the minister can give ?
How will the minister go about the purchase of the site ?
The officials of the department will purchase the site at the lowest possible price. If the price of the site chosen is not deemed satisfactory the property will be expropriated.
Is there any estimate as to what the site will cost ?
No. As in any other case, we obtain the site on the best terms, sometimes we ask the town in which the building is to be erected to contribute to the cost of the site.
Does the estimate the minister has given include the site as well as the building ?
Yes.
That is, the site and building together will cost, at the outside, $15,000 to $20,000 ?
Yes.

Of course, Sydney Mines is an important and growing place, largely for the reason the minister have given, namely, the development that has taken place through the operations of the Nova Scotia Steel and Coal Company. It seems to me, however, that the better course to pursue in matters of this kind is that which used to be followed some years ago by the department. The minister should give the House the plans of the proposed building and some more accurate estimate of the cost than my hon. friend the Minister of Public Works has been able to give. The House having been in session for so many months, one would think that, this estimate being now brought down, a little more information might accompany it. I do not see, for my part, why the estimate should not have been included in the main estimates, if we are to have no more information than that now given us. I am not objecting to the vote because I know this is an important town and one that, I believe, will largely increase in population. But I do think""it is a little irregular for the minister to come down with practically no information either as to the plans or as to the cost of the building.

It has been the custom of the Public Works, or, at least, for many years, to provide for new works in the supplementary estimates of the year. As I said before, I do not see how the department could either procure a site or make plans and estimates until it is authorized by parliament to proceed with the work. I do agree with my hon. friend (Mr. Borden, Halifax) that there ought to be as definite information as possible as to the cost of any proposed work. Under the advice of the chief architect I think I am safe in stating that the outside cost will be $20,000.
408i
In giving information, the main point to be considered and observed, it seems to me, is that parliament and the country should be advised as to the total expenditure that is to be undertaken. I have found fault in the past with ministers who have failed to give that information, but I think that when it is given the information as to details is not so important.

I may be permitted to say, in regard to the procuring of a site, that I have given some little attention to the matter and have made inquiries about it. I have the assurance of the general manager of the Nova Scotia Steel Company-and the rapid growth of the place is largely clue to the enterprise of that company-that a site can be secured for a reasonable amount. I am not authorized to say what figure they will ask, but I feel assured that the department will find the figure very reasonable indeed.
What is the size of the site V

When discussing the matter with the gentleman I refer to, I spoke of a site about 100 feet square, which I thought would be a fair size. I need not say anything of the necessity for this building, for that is generally recognized. I think the work had better be proceeded with at the earliest possible moment.
Better get the plans first.
Better get the money first.
The minister tells us that $15,000 or $20,000 will purchase the site and construct the building. Does that estimate include heating and other equipment ?

I think probably it would.
Halifax quarantine station, Lawlor's Island-improvements, renewals, repairs, &c., $4,500.
What is the need of this work V

This includes partitions and other changes in the detention building; rebuilding wails of hospital ward, detention building; fitting up two rooms in the hospital; and general repairs. There is due for plumbing, $1,700, which comes out of this vote of $4,500. The money was spent, not for new plumbing, but for overhauling plumbing which was out of repair.
I suppose that work was done by tender ?

No. That was not fopnd possible. The work was done under the superintendence of Mr. Dodwell, the engineer of the department in Halifax.	.

Halifax-new Public Building, $20,000.
This , is for work now under contract.
Wliat is tlie total cost of tliis building ?
The total probable cost of this building, exclusive of site, will be $318,000.
How much will the site cost ?

The site was purchased some years ago at a cost of, I think, $25,000, if I remember.
The MINISTER OB' PUBLIC WORKS. Twenty-four thousand. I find that the $318.000 is the estimated total cost including the site.
When is it anticipated that, this building will be finished-/
The contract calls for its completion on tlie 15th September, 1904. There was some delay, but the chief architect tells me that they are making very good progress now.

I have not been in Halifax for a good many months, and I do not know from observation what progress they are making. The progress did not seem to be very rapid up to the time I left. I suppose this vote of $20,000 is in addition to a vote already in the estimates ?
Yes.
How much is the total vote ?
One hundred thousand dollars.
Is it anticipated that the work will be finished at the time fixed for completion ?
The chief architect thinks it very doubtful if the work will be finished by the 1st September, 1904, but he thinks it will be finished by the first of the following year.
What departments of the public service will be accommodated by this building ?

This is nominally a customs house, but the building will also be available for other branches of the public service. No building lias been erected for the general offices of tlie Dominion in Halifax since confederation. The officers of the Dominion have been in the building which was erected before the union, and various buildings have been rented from time to time for the accommodation of the public service, but no general public building has been erected since confederation. This is intended to meet the Hon. Mr. SUTHERLAND.
difficulty and to obviate the necessity of renting buildings for the different offices. Though it is called the customs house, it will also provide accommodation for other officers of the public service.
How many stories will the new building be ?
Four stories above the basement.
Will there be an elevator ?
Yes, two elevators.

I suppose no arrangement has been made as to which of the officers now in the other building will be removed to the new building. Of course, the customs house officers will go. The post office, I suppose, will be continued in the present building ?

As the post office is very much cramped now, the intention is that it shall have the main floor of the present building, which is at present divided between the post office and the customs house, the customs being entirely transferred to the new building, and probably the Marine and Fisheries Department also. Except as to the customs no definite policy has been determined upon, although I think it will be found convenient to also transfer the Marine and Fisheries Department to the other building. The idea is to afford the customs house sufficient accommodation in the -new building, to give the space made by the removal of the customs house from the old building to the post office, and then to distribute the rest of the space amongst the other officers. A portion of the present post office might be assigned to the savings bank, which is now in a private building, and that will give the bank a front upon Hollis street, which is in the centre of the business district of the city. Subject to that qualification that we hope to give the post office the space which was formerly divided between the post office and the customs houSe.

If I remember rightly on an upper floor of the present building there is a collection of some objects of interest in connection with the province of Nova Scotia. It is at present in a very inaccessible place.

The museum has been removed. While it occupied the Dominion building it was always a question whether it belonged to the province or the Dominion. The province owned the museum, but it claimed that it had the right to a place for it in the building. For a long time the museum occupied a place in this building, but the local government procured accommodataion for it in the old Burn-s building opposite,

the museum has been transferred to that building, and I believe that under the care of Mr. Piers it is now in very good condition. X do not know what the space thus vacated in the old building is applied to at present, but while in that building the museum was inaccessible and unsatisfactory in all respects.
Halifax immigration building - additional story over the one story portion, &c., $11,000.
What is that for ?

The improvements to this building are being made at the request of the immigration branch of the Interior Department. An additional story is being put on the one story part of the building. It has been represented that they had not sufficient accommodation for immigration work and on account of these representations the improvements are being made.
What is the additional accommodation required for ?
More accommodation is required for immigrants. This is partly a one-story and partly a two-story building, and we are putting a second story on the part which is now one story.
I think I saw in one of the newspapers that some examination had been made of this building, and that it had been reported unsuitable. Is not that the case ?
It lacks sufficient accommodation.

Is it because the examination which has been made of the building by some official or officials that this additional vote is being asked ? I do not know anything about it, except that I saw it referred to in the public press.

In regard to buildings of this description which are under the control of other departments, we go very much on the representations of the officials in particular charge of the work. No information is given to the chief architect or to the deputy minister to show that the building is not in good condition, and suitable for the accommodation of this branch of the service, but the trouble is that it is too small. Since this matter has been considered, we have had further representations made to the department that even with this proposed improvement there will not be sufficient accommodation. But, as far as I know, the accommodation they have is very good.

This application was made by the Department of the Interior on behalf of the immigration branch, during the present session of the House, and it has recently appeared that
these representations are confirmed and that more accommodation is needed.
By whom was this examination made ?

I think it was by some medical gentleman connected with one or other of the provinces. I forget whether it was by an official of our own government or not. At all events it was stated in the public press that there was a need of greater accommodation, and when I noticed it I was glad to know that the Department of the Interior had already asked for this accommodation, and that the hon. Minister of Public Works was about to provide for it.
Will the additional story be constructed by tender and contract ?
Yes, I may say that. We are to expend $11,000, and it is quite a sufficient work to have detailed plans drawn and the work let by tender.
Is $11,000 expected to be sufficient to complete the work ?

The chief architect informs me that it is sufficient according to the plan.
Digby public buildings-improvements, $1,800.

This provides for a clock in the tower, and some improvements in the public buildings.
Antigonish-new fittings for post office, $1,500.

This is for general improvements. Some of the floors are in bad condition and the letterboxes are very old. This is to provide new floors, screens for the public lobbies, two hundred new letter-boxes, and general repairs to the building.
What kind of letter-boxes?
They will be the ordinary brass letter-boxes.

I have noticed different kinds of letter-boxes, some very much more convenient for the use of the public than othf rs. I have seen some in the Northwest which are a great improvement on any that I have seen down here. The letterbox which I think should be put in is one to which the owner can have access at any time without having to go to the wicket to inquire.
We are putting in the improved kind.
Who supplies the boxes ?

Rubenstein & Co., of Montreal, make the most of the boxes for the department.

Sydney-addition to public building (revote, $5,000), $10,000.

This is to provide an addition to the present building 40 feet by 30 feet, with two stories, attic and basement. It is represented to be necessary on account of the growth of the place. The postal revenue is between $17,000 and $18,000 and the customs revenue about $150,000, and the money orders issued amount to nearly $200,000.
Is this to be the entire cost of the addition ?
No, the total cost is estimated by the chief architect at $15,000.
How is the work to be done-by tender and contract ?

Yes.
North Sydney public building, $1,100.

This is for general improvements. Some of the brick walls are out of condition, iron columns have to be taken out and some doors changed, modern letter-boxes are to be placed in the building, and other repairs are to be made.
Charlottetown armoury-additional accommodation for orderly rooms, &c., $2,550.
This has been expended by the department in accordance with a request from the Department of Militia.
Are all mililia expenditures by the Department of Public Works made on the requisition of the Militia Department ?
I think all of them. I do not know of any exception.
Is this work going on at present ?
Yes, it was undertaken some time ago, and is practically completed.
This work was very much required, and I must compliment the department on having it done.
Is the work done by contract ?
No, it is done under the superintendence of the militia officer in Charlottelown.
Who did the work ?

I have the details of the cost of the work, but not the names of the different parties who did it. I would be pleased to have a Hon. Mr. SUTHERLAND.
memorandum made giving the information the hon. gentleman asks for. I imagine that it was so general that the militia officers did the overseeing themselves.
That is a new role for militia officers.

I am not sure that it is not a good plan, as they have an interest in seeing that the work is well done.
Charlottetown Dominion building-improvements, additions, &c. (revote, $8,000), $12,000.

This is for the construction of an annex in the rear of the Charlottetown Dominion building, also for alterations, repairs and renewals. The estimated cost is $12,350.
Mi'. LEFURGEY. Is this annex something new put in the estimates this year ?
No, there was a vote taken for this some time ago.
Has this annex been proceeded with yet ?

No ; the plans were prepared and tenders
advertised for, and the contract was let a short time ago.
To whom was the contract let, and at what figure ?
The tenders were received only a few days ago and the information is now in my notes. The deputy does not remember the name but I will bring it this afternoon.
Has the lowest tender been accepted ?
The lowest tender was accepted.
What is this annex to be used for ?
Generally in connection with the post office.
It seems to me that this is a large amount for an annex to the post office in Charlottetown.

I had myself the pleasure of being in Charlottetown a year or two ago and complaint was then made of the lack of accommodation in the post office. I am told that the improvement is very urgently required. I think almost all of the officers connected with the department are in the one building. It contains the post office, savings bank, customs and inland revenue offices, weights and measures office and the marine office. I think this addition is being made principally <>n the strong recommendation of the postmaster there, Mr. Brecken, an old friend of ours who used to be in this House. He

lias written to me several times in connection with this matter since I have been in office.
Mr. CLAItKE. Will this vote cover the amount of the tender ?
The	MINISTER	OE	PUBLIC	WORKS.
The amount we are now asking will cover it. There is a re vote of $8,BOO and a new vote of $4,000.
Mr.	CLARKE.	Will	this complete the
annex ?
The	MINISTER	OF	PUBLIC	WORKS.
It will complete the work.
Public buildings, New Brunswick-Oampbell-ton public building, $5,000.
The	MINISTER	OF	PUBLIC	WORKS.
An application was pressed on the department for a public building at Campbellton, New Brunswick. I looked into the matter personally and found that it was quite a growing and thriving place. The postal revenue has increased until last year it was nearly 84.000 and the customs duty nearly $7,000. It is a seaport town and the business has very largely increased :	I
thought I was warranted in asking parl'a-ment to authorize me to construct a public building there.
What will the'total cod be ?
Between $20,000 and $25,000.
What will be the price of the site V
I cannot give the price of the site as it has not yet been purchased.
What is the population of Campbellton ?
About 7,000.
I am sure it is not 7,000.
I am sorry to say I have not the population here.
Have the plans for the building been prepared V
General plans have been prepared.
General plans for this building, and these plans show that the building will cost $20,000 or $25,000 but the site has not yet been looked up.

It has not yet been purchased. I may say that if parliament authorized me to undertake any public building and I found th.it the price asked for a site was not reasonable I would not go on with the work. 1 think that parliament has a right to expect to acquire a site at a reasonable price. Such as other people would have to pay. We all
know that when the government undertake a work people seem to think they can get an exorbitant price for their property. 1 have several times taken the position that if I could not acquire a site at a reasonable price I would not go on with a work and have found it to work satisfactorily.

Campbellton is a terminal point on the Intercolonial, a very large seaport town with large shipping interests, with large lumbering operations, and it is also the centre for a large section of New Brunswick and for a section of Quebec. A portion of Bonaventure is tributary to Campbellton and its business centres in that town. It is a very enterprising town ; there are large milling establishments and it is deserving of recognition in this way if any town in the Dominion of Canada is deserving.

Will this be put under contract and tender or will it be done by the department '!
I think this can hardly be done by tender.
The preceding item will I suppose be by tender ?

Tracadie Lazaretto-improvements, ae., $1,500.
This vote is asked to make provision for a small steam disinfector. We had application from there for a number of other improvements but we thought they might stand in the meantime.

Does the minister know anything about the condition of the Lazaretto and how many persons are afflicted with leprosy. Are they increasing or decreasing ? This Larazetto has been in operation for a long time and it is nearly time that the disease was cleaned out of that locality.
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS, 'file lion, gentleman might renew his question when the estimates of the hon. Minister of Agriculture are under discussion.

Has the govern-men any information as to whether th;s disease is increasing or decreasing in Canada ? Statements are made from time to time in the public press as to its increase and it would be desirable for us to know whether there is any official information which can be communicated to the House with regard to it.

As I said before it. will perhaps be better to ask this question when the estimates of the Minister of Agriculture are under Consideration.
provide a new building. Since then we have been informed by the Militia Department, which has requested this expenditure, that there is a building there which can be utilized, with some alterations and repairs. So, this estimate of $5,000 is proposed, which, it is expected, will cover the expenditure for the present year. The total cost is estimated at $11,000.
Will the work be done by contract ?
Yes.

I may state in answer to the inquiry that leprosy has been decreasing for some years in that locality. Sometimes when the doctors grow jubilant in the belief that no more cases will be found, a case may arise in a family which has been free frem it for a generation. The children escape the disease, but their children become its victims. Still the number is decreasing. When this Lazaretto was transferred to the control of the Dominion government there were about twenty-three or twenty-f ur cases, but now the number arising in the locality is fourteen or fifteen. The number has been added to by the importation of three or four cases from British Columbia and Manitoba, and I believe that one of these died last year.
How many are there altogether ?
I do not know the exact number, but I believe it is about 19 or 20, of whom 14 or 15 are from the locality. I believe that the Department of Agriculture has all that information.
Of what nationality are the people who were brought from British Columbia ?
Swedes or Norwegians, I believe.
No Chinese among them ?
No. I believe that the Dominion government refused to accept the Chinese for this Tracadie hospital.

It would be advisable that the Department of Agriculture should be ready, when its estimates are before the House, to explain how the lepers were transported across the continent and tvliat means were taken to disinfect the cars in which they were carried.
The disease is not contagious.

The hon. gentleman (Mr. Emmerson) is mistaken.

St. John Immigrant building, $10,000.

This is to provide additional accommodation in the St. John immigration building. The estimates as originally prepnred to meet the requirements of the immigration department provided for a two-story addition to the present building, to cost $6,500; furniture, $1,500 ; superintendence and incidentals, $2,000; making a total of $10,000. But, this estimate was made before the fire took place in the freight shed of St. John, burning part of this building. This will make necessary a new arrangement, but it is estimated that the sum of $10,000 will still cover the cost. I understand that a joint arrangement is made between the Canadian Pacific Railway and the Interior Department for an extension.
That will probably be a further supplementary estimate.
No, I understand that this is to cover the cost of repairing the damage done by the fire, as well as the improvements ?
All the expenditure by the Public Works Department will be covered by the amount I have stated.
Will the work be done by tender and contract ?
Yes, our work will be let by contract. There may be some small repairs outside of the contract, but this contract will cover the main part of the work.

Permit me to draw attention to a point which was under discussion a little while ago-the public building in Campbellton. Now, Campbell-ton is a nice little village. The hon. member for Westmoreland (Mr. Emmerson), as I understand it, stated that the population was 7,000.
I said 7,000.

The whole population of Restigouche county is about 10,000 and Campbellton is between 800 and 1,000.
New Brunswick-Woodstock public building -improvement, $3,900.
The MLmoTGR OP PUBLIC WORKS. This is to provide for new letter-boxes and to make some repairs to the building.
Is tbis the drill shed again ?

No, this has nothing to do with the drill shed. We have a public building in Woodstock. About $2,000 had to be spent in repairs, including the building of a retaining wall.
Mr. BORDEN fHalifax). Has the work been done by contract or by day labour ?

There will be a contract for the boxes, which will be the principal amount. The work already done was done by day labour.
Fredericton military buildings-officers' stables (revote, $1,500), $2,400.

This is to build a stable in place of one that was demolished as useless. This is under contract now. The revote of $1,500 was not paid out at the end of the year. It is let by contract to C. J. B. Simmons.
Fredericton military buildings-Sergeant-major's quarters, $2,300.
This is a revote of $1,000 and $1,300 additional, and is to make provision for the sergeant-major.
How many sergeant-majors are there ?

I suppose there is only one, but he may have a large family. I think it includes sergeants as well as the sergeant-major.
St. John quarantine station-water service, &c., $7,000.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: The total cost is estimated at $24,000. We had a long discussion on this quarantine station when the main item was up. This is simply a revote of an amount which was not spent at the end of June last. The station is on Partridge - island. The water supply comes from the city.
Can you not get an adequate water supply on the island ?

I am told by the deputy minister that they have expended a lot of money in sinking
artesian wells, and they cannot get any fresh water.
Has that quarantine station been used at all ?

I cannot give the details I would like to. This expenditure is made by the Department of Public Works at the request of the Department of Agriculture. I have no doubt that in the winter time -this is much used.
I presume the minister has taken precautions that the pipe should not form an obstruction to vessels when the tide is low. There was some difficulty in Toronto on that account.

The work is Ibeing done under the supervision of the engineer for the province of New Brunswick, and I presume he will look after that.
St. John drill hall, $10,000.

This vote is put in at the request of the Department of -Militia and Defence. Judging from my experience of such buildings in other places, I would not take the responsibility of saying -that this building, when completed, will cost less than $100,000. The drill hall in Windsor cost $75,000 and that in London considerably more. I do not believe a suitable drill hall in the city of St. John could be erected for less than $100,000 in round figures.

I wish to make a correction of a statement I made with respect to the population of the town of Campbellton, which I gave from the impression I obtained from visiting it and seeing that it was an important place. I find that Campbellton has a population of about 3,000. It is an incorporated town, and comprises almost the whole of the parish of Addington, in the county of Restigouche. It has been incorporated for a number of years, and has a mayor and council and a water system.
It is an ocean port, is it not V
Yes.

When the hon. gentleman makes a statement in the House that the town has a population of 7,000 inhabitants, when at -the outside it has not more than 1,200, naturally I feel a little delicate in pointing out that the hon. gentleman is in the wrong. He says that it is incorporated. It is not incorporated ; if it was, it would be put down in the census as incorporated.
It is incorporated by special Act of the legislature of New Brunswick, and has been for a number of years.
If it was incorporated as an ordinary town, it would be put down in the census as a separate municipality, whereas it is not mentioned in the census as a separate municipality.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
speechtext: We have passed the item for Campbelltou, and the hon. member for Westmoreland (Mr. Em-inerson) having made his explanation, we cannot say any more on this item.

I would like to get some more information about this St. John drill hall. The Minister of Public Works has told us, with his psual candour and lucidity, that it is likely to cost $100,000. Have we got a site purchased yet ? Have we any engineer's estimate ? Do we know where we are at ? He is asking us for $10,000, not knowing what the ultimate expenditure will be.	[DOT]

I was about to explain to the committee that a site had not yet been purchased. Some of the officers in St. John think that a new site should be purchased and that the government land should not be used. Others of the officers are of the opinion that a site located upon the land at present owned by the government is satisfactory. I have not had an opportunity yet, personally, to look into the question, but I intend to do so at an early date. I am not able to offer an opinion, but we have a good deal of land which was formerly occupied by the British government for military purposes and handed over to the Dominion at the time of confederation, and I had hoped that it might be possible to find a suitable site on that land. The cost of a suitable drill hall for a city like St. John cannot be less than somewhere about $100,000. That would be the figure I would name. Cities of similar population, such as the city of Halifax and other cities, have had drill halls erected at somewhere near that amount. The Halifax drill hall cost a good deal more-probably more than it ought to have cost. I will put the cost somewhere between $50,000 and $100,000, not to exceed $100,000.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Have there been any plans prepared yet ?
We have had general plans for such a building, but the particular plans that would! be used in the city of St. John have not yet been completed.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: It would cost from $50,000 to $100,000 ?
Yes.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: How many regiments have their headquarters at St. John?

There is the 62nd, a large infantry regiment, and there is a large garrison artillery regiment. I am not sure that there is any other regiment at present at that place, but in addition to that there are the field hospital and the bearer company.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: In connection with these estimates, if the bon. Minister of Public Works would take a suggestion from me, he would come down and tell us the amount that it will take to complete the building. I have in my mind cases in which some innocent looking estimates have come down for a few thousand dollars, and the expenditure terminated in about ten times as much as it wTas expected the building was going to cost. I think the question of the cost of a public work should be settled by the department before the hon. Minister of Public Works comes down and asks for any money at all. I do not think it is necessary to take the whole amount at first, but it appears to me that it would be more satisfactory to the committee to first determine the cost and then to carry out the plan as originally intended. In this case, they tell us that the building may cost $100,000, and they are only asking for $10,000 to commence with. The hon. Minister of Public Works will remember some similar cases in which small amounts were first asked, but in which the buildings cost a great deal more than the committee anticipated before they were completed.

I had thought that I should rather have received a compliment from the hon. member from Nortnumberland (Mr. Cochrane) than criticism. He and I are agreed that such a full statement should be given of a work that is intended to be undertaken that parliament cannot be deceived, and I think in this case that I have only been carrying out my promise to the House in that regal'd. These works are undertaken on the representations of the Department of Militia and Defence, and they have estimated that the cost of this building will run between $50,000 and $100,000.
The hon. Minister of Public Works states that this building is now estimated to cost between $50,000 and $100,000. Has there been any estimate made?

The department in preparing the plans has the experience of the cost of buildings similar to the one which it is now proposing to erect. The department, having stated that the cost of the building will not exceed $100,000, if the plans are not in accordance with that estimate, it has no right to go on with the work'.
What did the Halifax drill hall cost ?
Speaking from memory, it cost betweeu $250,000 and $300,000.
Why is it estimated that you are going to provide St. John with a drill hall with an expenditure of from $50,000 to $100,000?

I think they have other accommodation in St. John. Our effort, which is seconded by the Department of Militia and Defence, is to try and keep down these large expenditures as much as possible and to spread the expenditure more wisely over the country. If we can get sufficient accommodation for a reasonable expenditure, I do not see why we should go to any more expense than is really necessary.

Would it not be a better business proposition for the Department of Militia and Defence, if they want a drill hall at St. John, to ascertain what the strength of the force that will require accommodation is likely to be, and then prepare plans and give the committee the actual information as to what the cost will be ? In four or five cases this morning votes of $5,000 or $10,000 have been asked for public buildings, and when we have asked if a site had been procured or if plans had been prepared, we have been answered in the negative. The department are in blissful ignorance as to what the cost will be, and we have to go it blind. Of course, we can assume no responsibility for such a lavish and reckless expenditure as this.

I hope my hon. friend will not object to this vote. It is not a large vote. It is true that all the data may not be forthcoming that ought to be available, but I think the committee can trust the minister and the government not to proceed with any expenditure until all the information has been obtained that is necessary, and until proper plans have been made. I am satisfied that additional accommodation is necessary at St. John. Recently the district. officer commanding that district has been moved from Fredericton to St. John. Therefore, it has become a more important military centre. I am satisfied that if proper accommodation is provided the active militia at St. John will be increased, and I think it is desirable that at a point like St. John, which is a point of strategical importance, the strength of the militia should be increased. It will not be increased until sufficient accommodation is forthcoming. I will hope that as an earnest of what is intended my hon. friend will not object to the vote of $10,000. My hon. friend will find in the estimates later on an item which he will approve of, an item for the extension of the drill hall at Toronto. The necessary plans for the expenditure of that vote have not yet been matured. It is in very much
the same position as the vote for St. John.
I hope, therefore, that my hon. friend will not object to this.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: I am' sure the Minister of Militia does not want to misrepresent my course in this matter. We do not object to constructing drill sheds at these different strategic points, but we think it is very bad strategy and very bad business for the government to come to parliament and ask for a vote of $10,000 for a building which *every one knows will cost perhaps ten times more, and at the same time, give us no information whatever about the matter. We want to know what kind of a building it will be ; what it will cost; whether a site has been purchased and what is its cost, and whether the municipal authorities of St. John have been approached with the view that they might donate a site. All this information should be given by the government.
They do not know even where the building is to be situated.

As a matter of fact the government give us no information whatever, although they are pledging parliament to what may ultimately be a very large expenditure. I might be called to order were I to discuss the item further on in the estimates for the extension of the Toronto drill hall, but I may say here that the militia force of the city of Toronto will appreciate the action of the minister in asking an appropriation of $20,000 for that purpose. Whether the vote is sufficient or not, I cannot say at the present moment, but if the department has not had proper plans prepared for the extension of the Toronto drill hall they are open to just the same criticism as in the case of the St. John drill shed. What we object to is that -we are voting this money practically in the dark.
I must take exception to that.
To this method of doing business ?

No. It is impossible for us to do what the hon. member (Mr. Clarke) suggests. We cannot purchase a site until wre are authorized by parliament to go on with the work, and purchase that site. Then, as to the character of the building, a good deal would depend on what site is selected. It is impossible to ask the chief architect to draw a plan, except in a general way for a public building, until he knows on what kind of ground it will be erected. We are asking here for authority to undertake a certain work, and we state what that work is estimated to cost, and there can be no deception in the matter whatever. I agree that if we ask for a further vote, after the original vote is taken, we should be able to give details.
Are we to understand that this money is to purchase a site ?

It can he used for that.
Mr.	HUGHES	(Victoria).	I	think	theminister will find that the present military property owned by the government at St. John	it not well	situated for a	drill shed.Mr.	CLARICE.	Why ?	-Mr.	HUGHES	(Victoria).	Because	the
land owned by the government is situated on the sea coast, and also because it is too far removed from the centre of the town.
That is what some of the military gentlemen in St John say.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: If the government property were selected, the men would have to walk from a mile to three-quarters of a mile from the centre of the town. I think the minister will find that it is advisable to build the drill shed in a more central location.
Not in the case spoken of to-day.

The only case cited to-day was the case of Halifax. Halifax is a city of not much more, importance than St. John-perhaps the hon. gentleman from St. John will not admit that it is of any more importance. A small sum was originally voted for the drill shed at Halifax, and year after year other votes have been taken, until the amount has reached nearly $300,000.
There has been a change of government since then.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: And I presume there will be another change of government before this building at St. John is finished, which might be a reasonable guarantee that the cost will be cut down. I have no doubt that the great cost of the drill shed at Halifax

is to a certain extent attributable to the change of government, while another change may work reform in the opposite direction. What we are objecting to is the principle on which this is done. The government ought to be able to inform parliament as to the site which will be chosen, and then if there is an architect of experience in the service of the department, he should be able to estimate within $10,000 or $15,000 the cost of the building.

That is exactly what we have done in this case. As minister, I should feel that if it were found that the expenditure would be considerably in excess of the amount which I stated to parliament, I would not go on with the work until parliament had sanctioned that change. I have always contended that it is wrong to do anything else, and I expect to have the support of my hon. friend (Mr. Bell) now. I have stated to the House about what the cost will be, but it is impossible to bring down a detailed plan until the site has been purchased.

I do not think, that the criticism of the minister on my course is justified. What I maintain is, that we should not be drawn into large expenditures by these small degrees. No business man or no business corporation would embark in an enterprise, under such circumstances as confront parliament in this case. The government do not know the cost, and actually, they do not know where they are going to erect the building.
But we are not doing that.

We have been told here today that this building will cost from $50,000 to $100,000. That is an enormously wide margin ; it is in fact no estimate at all. The Minister of Public Works would not transact his own business in that way. The procedure in this case is utterly unbusinesslike.

I do not think so. If you are putting up an addition to a factory and you know the maximum amount it will cost, then any business man would be safe in proceeding with the purchase of the site, and the details could be figured out afterwards.
Would a business man be satisfied that an estimate which varied from $50,000 to $100,000 ?

I quite agree that it would not be right to take a vote for $10,000, and after the statement is made that the work would only cost $10,000, then proceed to spend $100,000. But in this case, we have given the maximum cost as nearly as possible.

Then I suppose we must accept the statement of the minister ; that

so far as lie is concerned, and if he remains in office, he pledges the government to the staiement that this expenditure will not exceed $100,000; of which we are now asked to vote the first instalment of $10,-
000.

Having made the statement to the House that the estimated cost will not exceed a certain amount ; then, if when the plans are made out it is found that the building would largely exceed that amount, I would not feel justified in going on with it until I asked the sanction of parliament to the change. That is the position I take.

Will the $100,000 include the cost of the site ? The liou. member for Victoria (Mr. Hughes) points out, that because of strategic reasons, the government land is not suitable on which to erect this building ; and also because the men would have to walk a mile, or three-quarters of a mile, from the centre of the town to the drill shed, if it were erected on the property owned by the government. In view of this, another site may have to be purchased, and I would ask if the $100,000 estimate includes the cost of that site ?

One of the reasons why we have not decided as to the site, is that objection is taken to the land owned at present by the government as not being suitable. Perhaps the Minister of Militia might dispose of the government land if another site is purchased.
No, I do not think so.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: As the Militia Department has not come to a decision, of course, I cannot speak as to that.

We are fortunate in having both the Minister of Militia and the Minister of Public Works in the chamber at the present time, and I would ask, is it not a fact that the city of St. John offered a site some time ago, for the purpose of erecting a drill hall thereon ?

It is not a fact. There has been correspondence between the department aud the militia officers in St. John, and the department pointed out, that if it is not in the public interest to construct a building* on our own laud, then the municipality ought to provide a site. I regret to say that I have not discovered from the correspondence between the city authorities and the government, that there was any desire on their part to purchase a site and hand it over. A site has been selected by them which they would like ; it is not a very expensive site, but up to the present there is no agreement between the department and the
civic authorities as to who should pay for it.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: We do not object to having proper drill halls erected for the accommodation of our militia in the different centres of the country, but we do object to proceeding with such works without the government giving adequate information to parliament. We have in this case, a vote for $10,000. It goes to the public that this is all that will be voted for that purpose, and the electors never dream that in the end the cost may be perhaps $150,000. The Minister of Militia ought to be able to lay before the House all particulars with regard to this drill shed. This is a very loose way of undertaking a work of this kind. I am quite prepared to justify any reasonable expenditure for the accommodation of our militia force, but I cannot approve of the government proceeding in this way. The minister knows very well, that if we pass this vote now, there will be no hope of getting a site from the municipal authorities of St. John. If the government brings down a matured scheme there will be no difficulty in getting a vote passed through this House. We are not objecting to the expenditure of $10,000, or $100,000, but we do object that the country should be committed to a large expenditure without being placed in possession of the details.

I do not think it is desirable that we should threaten the city of St. John, that they will not get a drill hall, or a vote for one, until they agree to give us a site. If that is a good policy, then we have the cards in our own hands, and we can say : Unless you give us a site we will build on our own property. I can tell my hon. friend that I have satisfied myself that the present accommodation in the city of St. John is inadequate, and the military authorities have informed me of that fact. I have further satisfied myself, that a suitable drill hall can be erected for $100,000. We have general plans, which can be adapted to the city of St. John when the site is secured. It would seem to me that the information which has been given with regard to this vote, is far more ample than has been usually given with regard to similar votes. The criticism made by my hon. friend from Pic-tou (Mr. Bell) has no doubt a good deal of force ; but if he will go back during the whole time since confederation, he can apply that criticism to almost every public work that has ever been proposed in this House. I admit with him that it is a question for consideration ; but if we are to reform our course, I suggest that we put it off until next session, and allow this item to go through.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext:
I think I suggested that the argument I used was one which had been used not only by this, but by previous oppositions. I think I was laying down a sound

basis as to the mode in which these moneys should be voted, and I am glad to have the assurance of the hon. Minister of Public Works that he feels seriously disposed to look on the statement he makes in the House as made on his responsibility as a minister. I suppose we may consider that a limit has been fixed to this expenditure by one who is authoritative.
1 shall be able to tell. There is correspondence, and a site has been selected, which is approved of by the city and by some of the military men there. X think one of the military officers secured an option upon it in his own name. The government is in no way bound by that however. I presume that the price is named, bxit I do not remember it at this moment.

My own idea is that when a particular item is brought before the House, it should be explained at the time; but with regard to the purchase of a site for a public building, I think the proper plan is to be ready to close the purchase as soon as the land is selected, which could not be done if the minister had to wait till he could come to the House for a vote. With regard to a new drill shed for the city of St. John, I have no doubt that if the members from that city were here, they would admit the necessity of a new drill shed being erected in a suitable place in the centre of the populous part of the city. At present it is off at one side, and it is not convenient of access.
Is there a drill shed in existence in St. John now ?
Yes.
Is it practicable to use the site on which the present drill shed stands ?
Possibly it may be, although I think the department would first have to consider the question whether it might not be advantageous to dispose of that building and realize upon it.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Is the present drill hall up in the city cr down near the water front V
It is not in the centre of the city.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: There seems to have been some correspondence with respect to the site. Perhaps the government could tell us what amount of money this site will cost.
There is mo correspondence in the Public Works Department except what we have had with the Militia Department.

The Minister of Militia said that there had been some correspondence between his department and the municipal authorities, and that the site had partly been selected. If that site or ..some other like it is to be purchased, what amount of money will be required for it ?
I am not able to give my hon. friend a figure; but I will make a note of it, and when my own estimates come up Mr. BELL.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

I think they do.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

Not necessarily As I have already explained, the government own land there. I do not care to give an opinion with reference to it, but a very prominent officer in the city of St. John has assured me that the land owned by the government is perfectly suitable for a drill hall, and I propose to investigate that question carefully by sending down an officer from the headquarters staff before I advise the Minister of Public Works to purchase a new site.
air. EMMERSON. Before this item is passed, I would crave the indulgence of the committee to make on explanation, although it is not in order. speechtext: Early in the session I drew the attention of the minister and of the House to the necessity of having not only stores at various points, but also arsenals, and I pointed to the example set to us by the United States. All their arsenals are inland ; Springfield is in the centre of Massachusetts, and Rock Island is on an island in the Mississippi. Nearly all their private manufacturing arsenals are located remote from the sea-coast in order that in case of necessity they can lie used by the United States government. It would be really advisable that arsenals should not be established even in Toronto because it is on the coast of Lake Ontario. They would be better at inland centres, at Ottawa, or some place remote from the shore..

Yes ; I explained that this was au additional vote.

We do not need to purchase it, unless we have to pay the Department of Railways and Canals, in whose name it is now held.
Has the minister received tenders for this building ?
Not yet. I explained that there had been delay in making over the site from one department to the other.
Does the hon. minister know when he will commence construction on the building ?
I am sorry there has been delay, but I think we ought to be able to begin at once.
The Minister of Militia made some statements with regard to buildings in London and Toronto, in which military stores, ammunition and military sup-lilies, are to be stored.

I think my hon. friend (Mr. Clarke) misunderstood me. In these estimates we are asking, I think for the first time, to make provision for the establishment of stores buildings at different points throughout the Dominion.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Can the hon. minister give further information on the subject ?

There is provision in these estimates for the construction of a store building at Winnipeg and magazine at Toronto, a magazine at Winnipeg and a magazine at one other point, I think London. There is a general store building, as my hon. friend knows, at Toronto. Therefore, probably, any estimate for the construction of a building will be delayed for a short time.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: These magazines will be for arms and ammunition ?

For ammunition.
Quebec Citadel-drill shed for school of gunnery. $10,000.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: The estimated cost of this building is $30,000.
Is the school of gunnery permanently established at Quebec ?
Yes.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Is it a compulsory course ?

It will be. We have never had a suitable building for carrying out this sort of instruction, though it has been carried out, of course, to some extent. But now, in connection with the arsenal at Quebec, we are able to carry out the repairs of all the guns used by the artillery throughout the Dominion. If anything goes wrong with a gun we send it there, instead of having to send it back to the old country. We are putting in all the necessary machinery to repair the most delicate guns in use. It is, therefore, convenient to have a school of gunnery at that point. The very fact of carrying on this work of repair enables the teachers to illustrate and explain the different parts of the gun. We are having this building constructed, which will cost $30,000, to enable this to be done efficiently.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Of course, I understand this does not include instruction in musketry, but does it include light field guns as well as heavy guns ?
Guns known as guns of position -the 7'5 and a larger class of guns.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Would this include the guns used by -field batteries ?

Yes, field guns or heavy artillery.

1305a
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

Well, no ; that would hardly be included. Although it might be. This building would be sufficient to do that ; but I think that what is particularly had in view is training with reference to the different parts making up the field guns and larger pieces, and the use of such artillery.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Are you getting the new class of guns that have been adopted in the British army-the latest ?
Of rifle ? Yes ; we have ordered half a dozen of these guns, and we expect them here very shortly.

We are ordering them for the purpose of comparing them with our own rifle which is being constructed by the Ross Company.

A fifteen-pounder ? Mr. Haggart) refers to. We have ordered, subject, of course, to the decision of the War Office. I understand that the one likely to be adopted was the 18-5 pounder.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

No.	'

They should be delivered at the rate of 1,000 a mouth. I am told that before the end of the year they will be delivered.

Yes

Not as between the Lee-En-field and the Ross, but the Ross rifle is being manufactured so that all the parts are interchangeable. The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND

Montreal examining warehouse, additions and alterations, including fittings, furniture, &c., $20,000.

Mr. UIiAIN. I noticed when this matter was up last year the minister stated it would cost $30,000, now he says it will cost $35,000. Can the minister explain the reason of the different estimates ?

I do not know that there is any explanation that I could give. The difference is nut large in an estimate for repairing a large building like this.
Terrebonne, public building, $5,000.

This is t provide for the erection of a new public building in the town of Terrebonne. Although a small town with a population of only about 2,000, according to the last census. I understand it is the most important place in the district. The post office revenue is about $17,000. The money orders issued amounted to $9,670, and those received to $34,000.

The site has not been provided. The total
cost including the site will not be over

It is to be used for customs and excise as well as a post office.
Acton Vale public building, $6,000.
The MINISTER OF ' PUBLIC WORKS. This is a new building. I understand that Acton Vale is the principal town in the county of Bagot. The population according to the last census was 1,175. It is estimated to cost about $10,000.

It is refreshing to see a large stun like this voted for a public building in a village of the population mentioned, while the promise made by the Minister of Customs and others that the large oud flourishing town of Owen ' Sound should have a public building, has been entirely overlooked.
St. John's-public building, $6,000.

This building is to be used for the customs and other government officials as well as for a post office. It will be situated in the central part of the town. I believe there is no other public building in the country. If will cost about $10,000. The population of St. John's is over 4,000.
Does the minister say there are no other public buildings in the county ? What about the barracks?
I mean for a post office.
Further down in the same list I see there is a vote proposed for an examining warehouse.
Has the site been procured ?
The site has not been procured.
And the plans have not been prepared ?
Yes, they are prepared.
Of course, the work will be let by tender?
Yes.
Have there been any negotiations with or propositions from the municipality in respect to a site ?
No, I am informed there has been no correspondence in regard to that.
What proportion of this amount will go to a site ?
The deputy minister informs me that the site will cost over $1,000.
Will the balance complete and equip the building ?
The chief architect thinks that this amount will complete it, but my experience is that the fittings generally are extra.
Have they not a drill hall in St. John's already ?
They have a barracks, but no drill hall. They have a military school there.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: The plans of this building have been prepared. It was thought wise to prepare plans for this building and not wise to prepare plans for other buildings?

My hon. friend has misunderstood me. The plans were only prepared for this building because we are erecting similar buildings in other places. In speaking, of the St. John, N.B., drill hall, or of any other large building, it is necessary to prepare special plans, but in this case the plan which is available for other buildings only requires to be changed to suit the site.
Then, as a matter of fact, the plan has not been prepared ? It is a general plan ?

The plan is prepared for similar buildings,

and that is the plan we go upon in mating this estimate.
A model plan ?
A model plan.
What is the post office and customs revenue at St. John's ?
The postal revenue for the last year was $6,912 and the customs duties $119,549.
For Acton Yale also.
The post office revenue at Acton Vale is $838.
And the customs revenue at Acton Vale ?
It is an outport.
Is that not a pretty large building for an outport?
A public building there is only defensible under the policy which has been adopted of giving one building to the shire town of each county.
The case is a desperate one.

, There are just a few counties which have no buildings, and it seemed rather invidious to have these counties without a building. The policy which I have indicated was adopted rather to give the shire town or county town, as we call it, a public building ?
Why does not Owen Sound get one ?
What is the policy in respect of caretakers in public buildings in Quebec ?
In a great many cases the officer in charge lives in the building and takes care of the building at an average cost of about $60 a year.	.
Will there be a caretaker appointed for this building ?

I do not think that there is any doubt that the postmaster will be called upon to be the caretaker of this building, whether he lives in it or not. In some cases where the postmaster does not live in the building, he has to take care of it, for which he gets this allowance.

The building at St. John's and the building at Acton Vale are practically to cost the same?
409*

They are practically to.cost the same, but my hon. friend will notice that there is a very large postal and customs revenue at St. John's. It is now proposed to erect a new building in a more central part of the town for the accommodation of the people using the post office.
It is to be used for a post office only ?
Yes.

Assuming that it is, still the postal revenue of St. John's is eight or ten times as much as that of Acton Vale. If a building of that character is sufficient for St. John's, one would suppose a very much less expensive building would be needed for Acton Vale. What is the revenue at St. John's ?
Nearly $7,000.

Aud the revenue at Acton Vale is $838. Why should you have two buildings at practically the same cost ? If a building of this character is reasonably sufficient, and I have no doubt it is, for the post office at St. John's, where the postal revenue is nearly $7,000, upon what principle do you spend the same amount of money at Acton Vale, where the postal revenue is only $838?

If we had been putting up a government building for all the officials of St. John's, the building which we propose to erect would not be large enough, but this is wholly for a post office. At Acton Vale I do not think we could put up a suitable public building for much less than the figure I gave. The population of the town or village does not indicate the number of people who use the post office. People come in for half a mile or more from the surrounding country.

One would think that the postal revenue would indicate that. I think we started with the same premise that each of these buldings is to be used for the purpose of the post office. There is a separate building at St. John's for the custom-house. If you can erect a post office building at St. John's which is reasonably sufficient for the public needs for $10,000 to transact a business of nearly $7,000 a year, how is it that you are spending the same amount of money for erecting a post office at Acton Vale, where the total postal revenue is less than one-eighth of that amount ? I am afraid the hon. minister has not made himself very clear upon that point.

My hon. friend perhaps is right, but a man could build a house for the accommodation

of two people which would have the same capacity as a house built to accommodate ten people. When we want a certain number of offices of practically the same size, the difference in the cost of the two buildings is not material for that reason. I do not know whether we could expect to have a permanent and substantial building erected for much less money.
What rent does the government pay for the public building at present in use at Acton Yale ?
We do not pay any rent.
An allowance for rent is made to the postmaster ?
The post office is furnished by the postmaster, unless there is some special arrangement which I do not know of.
What allowance is made to the postmaster at Acton Vale for supplying the building ?
This is in the Post Office Department, and I know nothing about it.
It is information we should have when you are taking a vote for such a large sum for a public building.

This post office has a revenue of $838 a year, and probably the postmaster is allowed $50 a year for rent. Therefore, we are spending $12,000 for a building when we can rent a suitable one for $50 a year. And yet, in the town of Owen Sound, where the postal revenue is $14,500 a year there is to be no public building erected. This is a shame. The Minister of Customs (Hon. Mr. Paterson) should take some interest in this. He ran an election in North Grey one time, and he promised that Owen Sound should have a public building.

So far as I am personally concerned, I am prepared to admit that the town of Owen Sound should have a public building. There is no town in the province of Ontario, and no town that I know of in the Dominion, that is more entitled to a public building than Owen Sound. I am prepared to take that up later on.

Is it the intention of the government to bring down a vote this session for the erection of a public building in Owen Sound ? I gathered from a remark made by the Minister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Sutherland) earlier in the session, that it was the intention of the government to place a sum in the estimates for that purpose. I do not see any appropriation in this batch of estimates for Owen Sound, and I wish to know whether any further estimates will be brought down ?

1 do not think that the hon. gentleman (Mr. Thomson) will find any statement of mine in * Hansard ' to that effect. Speaking for myself, I said I was in favour of making a recommendation for an appropriation to erect a public building in Owen Sound, but it is impossible for me to say what will be in the estimates before they are published.

Owen Sound is entitled to some consideration from the Minister of Customs. His supporters promised during a certain by-election, that if the Minister of Customs were elected a public building would be given to the town. They voted for the Minister of Customs, but instead of getting a public building they got cold justice. The Minister of Customs is under an obligation to Owen Sound, to implement the promise of his supporters. I can assure him, that though he may fool the people some time he cannot fool them all the time, and if he goes back there for an election he is sure to get beaten.

It is to be regretted that the government have not submitted an appropriation for the erection of a public building in Owen Sound. In 1896, when the Minister of Customs (Hon. Mr. Paterson) came there to seek election, distinct promises were made that there would be a public building erected in Owen Sound if the hon. gentleman were returned, and in consequence of those promises he received a large majority. I regret to say that the riding of North Grey never received so few favours from the government, as when the . Minister of Customs represented it. At a later election, similar promises were made, and Dr. Horsey was returned. During the late by-elections supporters of the government swarmed the riding, and they declared openly that a public building -would be erected in Owen Sound if a supporter of the present administration were elected.
I may tell the Minister of Public Works, that notwithstanding that Owen Sound is Conservative, it gave a Liberal majority in 1896, for the Minister of Customs on the basis of the promises then made. There is a normal Conservative majority of from 100 to 150 in Owen Sound, and yet Dr. Horsey, in 1900 secured a majority. In the last byelection the promises were repeated and Owen Sound again gave a Liberal majority of 33. Thus, on three occasions, Owen Sound, although a Conservative town, gave a Liberal majority, because of the promises held out by the government. It is time that these election promises were done away with, and that Owen Sound should receive a public building on its own merits, irrespective altogether of political considerations. It shows base ingratitude to Owen Sound, that the government have not carried out their promises. The postal revenue of Owen Sound is about $15,000; the customs revenue, $40,000; the Inland Revenue, $100,000; and not-

withstanding that over $1,000 a year is paid in rents for the accommodation of the officers of the government, it is left without a public building; while a little place like Arichat, in Nova Scotia, with 600 inhabitants add $600 postal revenue gets a $22,000 post office. All through the supplementary estimates the same thing occurs; the government are erecting public buildings in small towns, and side-tracking an important commercial centre like Owen Sound. For instance, Campbellton. New Brunswick, with a population of 2,000 inhabitants, and a postal revenue of about $3,000, gets a public building costing $35,000, and the Minister of Public Works justifies his policy by saying that it is a seaport town and gives so much revenue. But, here is Owen Sound, with 10,000 inhabitants; with a postal revenue of $15,000 a year, and the Minister of Public Works, and the government of which he is a member, refuse to erect a public building in it. Well, the government have fooled the electors of North Grey two or three times, but they cannot continue fooling them for ever. When the next election -comes -around, the electors of Owen Sound will not fall so easily into the Liberal trap as they did on the past three elections, and the government will have to try some other electioneering dodge. I exceedingly regret the conduct of the government in this respect because I would far rather see Owen Sound with a post office and giving a Liberal majority, than without a post office and giving a Conservative majority. I hope that even at this late horn-, the government will bring down an estimate to erect a public building in Owen Sound, I trust that they will not longer neglect so important a town in the great province of Ontario.

I understood the Minister of Public Works to speak very nicely about Owen Sound, and to be in favour of giving a public building. Does lie intend to make any recommendation now, so that an estimate may be passed for the work this session ? Is it not time to fulfil the promises, solemnly repeated again and again to the electors of North Grey ? Surely the Minister of Customs will use his influence to get an appropriation for Owen Sound, which is one of the finest towns in Canada ?

I have no knowledge of any promise having been made with regard to the erection of a public building in Owen Sound. I did say, speaking for myself, personally, that I was in favour of the erection of a public building at Owen Sound. My hon. friend knows that I am not in a position to say just now what I can do. My hon. friend brought politics into the matter. I have no knowledge of that nor of any promise having been made. All I know is that the town of Owen Sound, from its commercial importance, is entitled on its merits to a public
building, and it will have my best assistance in that direction.

I have said all I desire to say about the town of Acton Yale. It seems to me that the building proposed to lie erected there is rather large, considering the revenue, especially as compared with the town of St. John's. My hon. friend the Minister of Public Works a moment ago said that he would take up the town of Owen Sound as soon as he came to it. What I cannot understand is why he -should come to the town of Acton Yale, which has a revenue of only $838, and a population of only 1,175, so long before he comes to the town of Owen Sound, with a postal revenue of $15,000, a large revenue from customs and excise, and a population of about 10,000.

My hon. frien'd must know that it is impossible for any minister to meet all the applications at one time. However, I have not changed my opinion with regard to the claims of Owen Sound.
Montmagny-public building, $6,000.
Is this a new building ?

No. This is an unfortunate building. It did not belong to the Dominion, and it collapsed in a storm. There were certain conditions with regard to it between the municipality and the department, which seemed to me to be objectionable, and I did not feel like rebuilding it unless those conditions were removed to some extent. It Is also a question for the chief architect to decide whether that would be the most economical course. I am taking this vote for the purpose of leaving the matter in the hands of the department, and seeing whether satisfactory arrangements can be made with the municipality. It will cost between $5,000 and $7,000 to -erect a building, and it would probably cost about the same amount to reconstruct the old building.
What is the population of that town ?
About 2,700.
Does the minister remember that some time ago there was $2,800 voted for that building ?
Yes, and the money was not spent for the reasons which I have just stated.

The minister should have sent an engineer to examine the building. In 1897 the member for that county at that time got $7,500 voted for the purchase of this building, and he knew very well from whom he was buying it. The building cost $7,494.75. That building was built on props, right over a mud hole, and that is the reason it went down last winter. There are many

buildings about it which did not go down. The fact is the man who put up that building was sick of it, and he sold it to the government five or six years ago. There is almost $5,000 gone, and the minister asks the House to vote $6,000 more ; that will be $11,000 for a population of 1,110.

I think we ought to have a fuller explanation from the minister after what the hon. member has said. Is it the intention of the government to erect another building on the same site or to purchase a new site ?

My hon. friend says the officials should examine these buildings. He will at least commend me for having taken action -in not spending money to repair it. The chief architect examined the property and reported this to me, and that is the reason this money was not spent before. Unless the conditions are changed, we shall not perhaps repair that building, but may find it more economical to build a new one. My hon. friend's statement is quite right, so far as I have been able to investigate the matter.

I would like to ask the hon. member for Dorchester (Mr. Morin) what he means by saying that the post office of Montmagny i-s erected over a mud hole and on piles, which I suppose he means when he speaks of props ?

In the first place, that building was not built for the post office. It was 25 or 30 per cent too large for that purpose. If I am not mistaken, it was used as a club or as a place where music was taught. If you put up another building there, do not build one as large as that.
Montreal post office-improvements, $13,000.

This is for putting in an elevator, improving the two passenger elevators, constructing a new street receiver, and making small repairs running from $400 down to $150.
St. Hyacinthe drill hall, $15,000.
The total estimated cost of this building as furnished by the MilStia Department is $24,000.
What regiment occupies this drill hall ?
The 84th regiment of infantry of St. Hyacinthe which is now a city battalion of four effective companies.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MILITIA AND DEFENCE.

speechtext: Has a site been purchased ?

No site has been purchased. Negotiations were going on some time ago for a very fine site, a large piece of ground on which we had an option at $4,000. A disastrous fire took place in the city, and the municipal
council approached us with regard to another site near the river. Negotiations for the purchase of the original site would probably have been concluded before now but for that fire.

I would like to have a statement prepared showing what drill sheds have been established in military centres in each of the provinces, giving by numbers the regiments occupying them, and the cost of each. I think that the province of Ontario has acquiesced in the spending of more money for this purpose in other provinces than in Ontario, although these provinces have not as strong militia forces as we have in Ontario.
I will get the information in detail, but I have some votes in Ontario coming up later on, and on them I will be glad to explain our policy in regard to this matter.

I notice that a small amount of money was voted in 1901 for the purchase of the site for this building. In 1902 that amount was increased to $5,000, and now we are asked for $15,000. This seems a strange condition of things as the $5,000 has not been spent and the site is not yet purchased. Does the minister regard that as being consistent with the principle he laid down last session, that he would deal with matters of that kind on business principles ?

I think my hon. friend (Mr. Blain) did not hear my explanation. When I asked for a vote of $5,000, we had an option for the purchase of a site, but after the disastrous fire in that city the municipal council I approached us with regard to the purchase of a site. If the original site is purchased, this would be all we could possibly spend between now and the end of the fiscal year. The estimated cost of the whole building is $24,000. My idea is that we will be able to prepare specifications, advertise for tenders, and start this work early in the spring, and that $15,000 will be all that we will require for the work to be done up to the end of the fiscal year. The balance will be asked for at a future session.
What amount have we to pay for a site ?
Four thousand dollars was the amount of the option we had on a site before the fire.
Is the proposition now to change the site ?

The municipal council proposed purchasing some property near the river, and they want us to take a portion of it. They have submitted a by-law to the people, and we are waiting for the result of that vote before we decide definitely on the purchase of a site. My hon. friend will understand that

in a large plade like that the government and the department are anxious to meet the views of the municipal council, representing the views of the people.

I think that this is a case where we can congratulate the Militia Department. The site has not been procured yet, but I understand the plans are ready. If the Militia Department had the plans ready in advance in some other cases, work would get on more rapidly. I commend the action of the Minister of Militia in having the plans of this building prepared in advance.
St. John's-examining warehouse, $3,500.

This is a revote of $3,500 to provide for the erection of an addition in rear of the St. John's public buildings for examining warehouse purposes. The present examining warehouse is an old wooden building set up on blocks ; neither wind nor water-tight; unfit for use and beyond repair.
Is this the same town in which the new public building is being erected ?	.
Yes.
Are there to be two distinct and separate public buildings there ? Why cannot they be combined ?
I explained that two or three times.
Why, the item has just been called, and I do not see how the hon. minister could have explained it.
I explained it on the other item, that for tlie post office building. This is an annex to the public building for >au examining warehouse.
When the department is putting up a new building cannot they make it sufficiently large to meet the requirements of this branch of the public service also ?
